title: Pair-Scan Run
statement: Let $m\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, let $h$ and $w$ be bit strings, let $\ell\in\{0,1,2\}$, and let $v$ assign a natural number to each of nine registers. Suppose every register value is at most $4|h|+4$, the limit register equals the pointer register plus $s_\ell|w|$, where $s_0=1$, $s_1=2$, and $s_2=4$, and, for every $i<|w|$, the bit of $h$ at position $v(0)+s_\ell i$ (taken as $0$ when out of range) equals the bit of $w$ at position $i$ (also taken as $0$ when out of range). If parsing $w$ as an aligned pair fails, the computation from the scan state reaches a false-answer state after advancing the pointer by $s_\ell t$ for some $t\le |w|$. If the parse succeeds with first component $a$, it reaches the scan-complete state with the pointer advanced by $s_\ell(2|a|+2)$. In either case, the computation invariant holds at every step before the reached state.

each sampled input bit agrees with the corresponding bit of $w$
